newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault has no comment on Sisu Oy talks.
newsitem.headline: Renault has no comment on Sisu Oy talks.

text.p: Shares in Renault SA, the smallest of Europe's Big Six carmakers, were weak on Monday amid concerns about the company's outlook, brokers said.
Renault officials were not available to comment on remarks by Finnish state-owned vehicle maker Sisu Oy that Renault might buy its truck business.

Pressure is high on Renault to line up partnerships to ensure its development amid prospects for slow industry growth in Europe and was heightened by last week's announcement that Volvo and Mitsubishi Corp were in talks to increase cooperation in trucks in Europe and Asia.
The Renault VI industrial vehicle division is closed until Thursday, and officials at Renault were not immediately available for comment.
Renault shares were down 0.80 francs, or 0.72 percent, at 110.20 at 1320 GMT. They hit a year low of 103 francs last week.
"Just because the share's weak doesn't mean people will buy," one trader said. "As the bourse gets more expensive, people are focusing more on fundamentals."
Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer said in a newspaper interview last week that he expected the money-losing trend seen in the first half to deepen.
"In a difficult economic context and taking into account the price war...I can only announce a strengthening of the trend," he told La Tribune.

He said the environment would be even tougher next year, with the European car market in slight retreat and the French market falling to 1.9 million car sales in 1997 from an estimated 2.1 million this year.
Renault has previously announced that it expects to report a loss for 1996.
